output.interpretation: Two-group comparison: human patient-derived pancreatic cancer (PDAC) organoids treated in vitro with a KRAS inhibitor (case) versus the same organoid lines treated with vehicle, usually DMSO (control). This would be human bulk RNA-seq with NCBI raw counts, both arms in the same GEO series and at least 3 samples per arm. The inhibitor could be a KRAS G12D-selective drug such as MRTX1133, a G12C drug such as sotorasib or adagrasib, or a pan-RAS/RAS(ON) drug such as RMC-6236 (daraxonrasib) or RMC-7977. No candidates are listed because I could not open any GEO record to confirm which samples are organoids and which are bulk RNA-seq, or to copy GSM accessions. GEO pages returned a browser check (reCAPTCHA) and the search tool's usage limit ran out. Leads to check by hand in GEO: (1) the bulk RNA-seq series behind the 2026 Cancer Cell paper on KRAS G12D-targeted therapy and interferon signaling, which used MRTX1133 on the PDAC organoid DAC-67 (GSE not found); (2) GSE293756 (MUC1-C/KRAS-inhibitor resistance), whose paper used patient-derived organoids; (3) the RNA-seq series behind the paper on MYC amplification and pan-RAS inhibitor (RMC-7977) resistance, which used human PDAC organoids (GSE not found); (4) the bulk series in the GSE315129–GSE315131 group (RMC-6236 with or without tazemetostat), to see whether any human samples are organoids rather than cell lines.

clarifying_questions.question: Which class of KRAS inhibitor should count as the treatment?
clarifying_questions.why: The drug classes act on different KRAS mutations, so pooling them changes the biology. A G12D-only scope limits the search to MRTX1133-type studies (e.g., the DAC-67 organoid work); a pan-RAS scope adds RMC-6236/RMC-7977 series.

clarifying_questions.question: Should only short-term treatment of drug-naive organoids count, or also organoids made resistant by long-term exposure?
options: Acute treatment (hours to days) vs DMSO only
Also include drug-resistant organoids vs parental
clarifying_questions.why: Several of the leads are resistance studies (e.g., stepwise MRTX1133 dose escalation, MUC1-C). In those, comparing resistant with parental organoids is a different question from treated versus vehicle.

clarifying_questions.question: If too few organoid series exist, can other model types be used as a fallback?
clarifying_questions.why: Most public KRAS-inhibitor bulk RNA-seq in PDAC uses 2D cell lines or xenografts (e.g., GSE302981 and the RMC-6236 bulk series). Organoids are not interchangeable with these, so including them changes which series qualify.

output.interpretation: Two-group comparison in human patient-derived pancreatic cancer (PDAC) organoids, bulk RNA-seq: case = organoids treated with a KRAS inhibitor (e.g., MRTX1133, sotorasib, adagrasib, RMC-6236/RMC-7977); control = the same organoids treated with vehicle (DMSO). I could not confirm any qualifying series. The GEO site blocked direct access to its records with a browser check, and my search tool ran out of uses before I could check the remaining leads. Because I could not copy sample accessions from GEO, I am not putting forward any candidates rather than guessing. The most promising lead to check by hand is the sotorasib + palbociclib PDAC study (Cell Death Dis 2025). It used a KRAS G12C patient-derived organoid (PDO-51T) and deposited RNA-seq as GSE301146 and GSE301148. Open those records and keep only PDO-51T samples treated with sotorasib vs DMSO, with at least 3 per arm. GSE279749 (PARP + KRAS G12D inhibitor, Nat Commun) and the data from the Fra-2/MRTX-1133 paper (PNAS) are also worth checking for human organoid arms.

From the sotorasib + palbociclib study, but it is the single-cell RNA-seq of mouse tumors treated with MRTX1133/palbociclib; wrong organism and assay.

Bulk RNA-seq from the sotorasib + palbociclib PDAC study, which used both cell lines (e.g., 51T-2D, a 2D line derived from an organoid) and PDO-51T organoids. I could not check on GEO whether the profiled samples are the organoids or the 2D/cell-line cultures, or whether there are at least 3 per arm. Check this by hand before using it.
Companion series to GSE301146 from the same study; same unresolved question of whether the samples are organoids or cell lines and how many replicates each arm has.

Single-cell RNA-seq of the immune microenvironment in pancreatic tumors after EZH2 + KRAS inhibition; not bulk organoid data.
